Welcome to the
2024 1-Card Print and Play Design Contest


ALL Results are IN!!
All entries are still in the geeklist, where you can find the latest information.

This contest aims to encourage the creation of innovative 1-card games in a variety of themes and mechanics. With this contest, we hope to sway all you clever and attractive* designers to create interesting new gaming experiences with the constraint of having... well... just 1 card.
And we also hope to hook all of you smart and beautiful* players and PnPers to be engaged in the creation of games for you, while being rewarded with awesome new games for your collection - for free!
Take a look inside the hood at how things are made, and help make them better!
* being clever, smart, attractive or beautiful is not a requisite to participate, but you all are clever, smart, attractive and beautiful anyway..! 
Any designer is welcome to submit an unpublished design  of your own, no matter if this is your first game or your 1,000th! The rules for the contest are listed below.
If you're a gamer or a PnPer, you can also participate by playing. giving feedback and even voting .
TL;DR: follow the entries that you like, print, play some games, give feedback to the designers, and then vote at the end of the contest for the games you played!
Anyone can actively participate and vote, the only requirement is to have a BGG account.
The contest was originally started by Joseph Propati, who ran it for 3 years. This will be the second year for Ben Morayta to host, hopefully in an acceptable manner. 
There aren't many changes this year from last, but if you're a veteran and missed last year's, please read carefully, as something might've changed from what you're used to!
All the contest information will be in the top post and first two pages of this thread, and will be kept updated.
If you have questions, check our FAQ (link below), ask on this thread by replying to this post, or send me a geekmail. I'll be glad to answer.

CONTEST RULES
Check the posts after this one to see the details on:
 Important Dates 
 Entry Requirements 
 Submitting an Entry 
 Components 
 Reference Sheet 
 Prizes and Categories 
 Voting 
 Copyright 
 Important information regarding AI and its use in this contest 

QUICK LINKS
 List of Entries in the Contest (official geeklist to enter)
 Prize categories start here (for results and winners)
 FAQ (Frequently Asked Questions) 
 Voting form is closed
 Results and Winners
 Playthrough Videos Geeklist (please add your videos to this list) 
 More links! 

IF YOU’RE NEW TO CONTESTS
 First time entrants may find it useful to view the   helpfully provided by Chris Hansen. Please ignore anything that has to do with GDCR, since we don't have that platform anymore.
 I also ranted a bit   and  . Feel free to take a look, but those two blog posts are just my personal opinion extended over [probably] too many words.

MOST IMPORTANTLY
The most important rule is: HAVE FUN!
These contests are great way to interact with fellow designers, play test their games and in turn let people play your game. Accept both positive and negative (constructive) feedback graciously, and give useful feedback in turn. You are not just participating in the contest, you are participating in the community.
Try to give more than you get. We all have different strengths and can help others more than you think (if only by playing their games and giving feedback).
Now go create some awesome games! 
If you're not a designer - well, you also have fun! That's the main objective of board games, and we all hope that you find our games worth your time and effort! (and if not, I apologize for us all...) 

This Contest's Discussion Thread
If you have comments, clarifications or complaints about these rules, please make a comment on the   thread.
There was ample discussion before the contest started, and maybe your question was already answered... but if not, we're always open for feedback on the rules, too, if not for this year, to improve the following contests.
In any case I'd prefer to keep this thread about the games and that other thread about the contest's rules. 
Thank you!

The contest rules are released under a Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial 4.0 International License. You are free to use and modify the rules for your own noncommercial contests or other projects. Please credit Chris Hansen as the original author when using these rules. This version of the rules was made by Ben Morayta and heavily based on John Kean’s 2-player contest.
This license applies only to the contest rules. It does not extend to the games entered or to the individual posts made on the contest thread.

IMPORTANT DATES

 Earliest Date for Games to be Publicly Available: January 1st, 2024
Any game that was publicly available online on BGG or other websites prior to the contest start date is not eligible for this contest.
See the entry requirements and the FAQ for clarifications on this point.
 Submissions: April 1st, 2024 to May 31st, 2024
New entries will only be accepted during the Submissions phase, but existing entries may be further developed after submissions close.
By the end of submissions, an entry must be playable, with components and rules available for download, though these need not necessarily be the final versions.
Any game still in Idea Phase will be removed from the entry list on that date.
 Development: Until June 15th, 2024
Games must be complete and final (Contest Ready) by the development deadline.
Any game that is not Contest Ready will be removed from the entry list.
After this date and until the close of voting PnP files and rules must not be changed, so that voters all have exactly the same version of the game to evaluate.
Players may still post feedback and suggestions (actually, are encouraged to do so), but fixes and adjustments cannot be implemented until after voting closes.
 Voting: July 1st to July 31st, 2024
A voting form will be made available at this time.
To vote, you should also aim to play as many games as you can, and you're encouraged to give meaningful feedback if you have any!
Results will be announced and prizes distributed shortly after voting closes.

text:
ENTRY REQUIREMENTS

Please check these requirements carefully to ensure that your entry is valid.

 The game should be exactly 1 poker-sized card (approximately 2.5 inches x 3.5 inches / 63.5mm x 88.9mm) 1- or 2-sided.
The preferred layout is in the center of the page - although other layouts are acceptable.
You may use both sides of the card. The back side of the card can be used for gaming purposes (i.e. both the front and back of the card is used in game play), a game logo, or be left blank (i.e. The games are not required to have a card back).
Designers will NOT be allowed to provide a larger sized card to the player, this scaling will only be left up to the player if they deem it necessary and will not be referenced or detailed in the rules as something the player must or can do on their own.
The single poker-sized card, however, can be altered (written, drawn on, cut, poked, folded, perforated, etc) as part of setup or during the gameplay, either temporarily or permanently. I know this part can be abused... please don't create a 54-card game where your card is cut into 54 mini-mini-mini-mini-cards (we don't have the sleeves for that  ), or a game where you have to redraw the whole layout of the card each turn. The idea of this contest is to have the challenge of making a 1-card game, so try to keep it in the spirit of the challenge. 
 There are NO RESTRICTIONS on theme, game length, components or art, or length of the rulebook.
However, it's worth noting that entries that are easy to play will probably attract more playtesters and voters.
 The rule book may have a reference sheet  as the last sheet in the rules for gaming information, charts, diagrams, and tables, but it may not be used as a game component.
This means you can't place components on it or have it act as a component during game play. (i.e. The player should be able to play the game without the rule book once the rules are learned yet can be referenced during play for rule refresher purposes.)
 Each game entered in the contest may optionally use up to a total 24 of the allowed components .
Click on the link for details on which components are allowed.
 The game must not have had components publicly available in any form before the Earliest Date for Games to be Publicly Available.
Games that were discussed elsewhere (but without the components being available), or that were distributed privately (for private alpha playtesting) before the Earliest Date are still eligible to be entered in this contest.
Games with a previous WIP entry, but that never went past an "idea", are eligible, but encouraged to create a new WIP post for this contest, to avoid confusion.
 The game must not have been entered in any other contest here on BGG, or in any other off-site contest. Games that were created through a challenge or design jam may participate (see details for restrictions).
Games that were entered in other contests but not completed (i.e. Withdrawn or Incomplete Entries, without components available) are still eligible to be entered in this contest.
Games that were drafted or created during a design jam or game design challenge, like the 24-hour contest here on BGG, or like the Game Crafter's challenges, are eligible to be entered in this contest, as long as they didn't place significantly on the original challenge (Finalists, top places, honorific mentions, etc are excluded from this contest).
 The game should not have had a game page on BoardGameGeek, or any other game database, before the contest.
Eligibility for games with a page created close to the start of the contest (and after the Earliest Date), or that didn't have activity before the contest will be decided on a per-entry basis; please send me a geekmail to review the details.
After entering the contest, you may submit the game to the BGG database without restrictions.
 The game must not be published (in retail, online, print-on-demand, or on any other form), or start the process of being published (signed/licensed with a publisher, with a crowdfunding campaign, started or not, or through any other means) throughout the contest and until after the end of the contest (when voting results are posted).
 Second edition games are NOT allowed.
A game that is inspired by, a sequel or a reimplementation of a previous game by the same author can enter the contest, as long as it's clearly a different game, with significant differences.
Mentioning the original game is optional.
 Each designer may submit any number of games by themselves or as a co-designer, but it's recommended not to submit more than 2.
All entries by a designer must receive attention, and the creators must interact with the feedback on all of the games. Because of this, entering more than 2 designs is discouraged, as it will take a lot of attention and work to complete them all, not to mention the requirement of giving feedback to 1 other entry per game entered (see below).
The host reserves the right to limit this mid-contest, if it's abused.
 Entries must have a WIP thread added to the geeklist (see main post for the link), and must be Components Available before the Submission Deadline and Contest Ready before the Development Deadline.
It's the designer's responsibility to keep the information and status for their entries updated with the latest changes.
 You may create a digital version of your game on TableTop Simulator, Tabletopia, PlayingCards.io or any online platform to facilitate playtesting, and link them in your WIP thread.
However, every game must also provide PnP files and a rules document, and keep them current.
Games should be judged and voted on the PnP version.
 For the benefit of all, entrants are required to play and post meaningful feedback on at least one (1) other game for each one that they enter.
If you enter two games, give feedback on two others. If you enter 3, give feedback on 3.
We will validate this requisite, and entries will be downgraded if the designer(s) didn't give enough feedback on other games in the contest.
Please reach out to me in private if you want to discuss this point.
If you give feedback outside of the game's thread (i.e. by geekmail, on comments on google drive, etc), please send me a note, so it's counted.

 The host reserves the right to make the final decision on any issues arising from the rules.

text:
"COMPONENTS
Each game entered in the contest may optionally use up to a total 24 of the following components. You must suggest the type and color of each component used in your games component list. You can also create a game without any components.
 Cubes. You may use any sized cubes metal, wood or plastic.
 Coins. You may use a different sizes of coins in your game. (i.e. a US dime, nickle, and quarter.) Be mindful of international players when designing games with U.S. coins.
 Paperclips. You may use metal, wood or plastic clips in a variety of colors or shapes.
 Discs/squares. You may use metal, wood or plastic any size.
 Meeples. You may use mini or standard sized single color meeples from games such as Carcassonne .
 Dice. You can use any of the following dice types; d4, d6, d8, d10. d12, and/or d20. These are the only dice types that will be allowed, a d100 will not be allowed so to create a % you will have to use 2d10 for % or 1 to 100. The dice can be of any single color and have pips or values on the dice faces.
 Crystals/glass beads. Versions that are commonly found in craft stores or other games may be used.
 Bags/cups. These can be used for randomly drawing other components. Bags/cups do not count toward the 24 component limit when used as containers. Bags/cups can not be used as a component or space for gameplay, only for randomizing.
 Timing devices such as hourglass, phone timer, kitchen timer are allowed and do not count as part of the component list when used to keep time. Timers can not be used as a component for gameplay.
 A pen or pencil. You can use a pen or pencil in your game, on your card or on a scrap piece of paper to keep score.
 Items found in a household, as long as their specific brand, type, size, color or shape are not restricted, and only if the main gameplay happens on the card itself, not on/around the items, can be used as part of your game (i.e. a book, as long as it can be any book, or a plate, as long as it's not a specific size or shape). Each item counts as part of the 24 allowed components.

For each of the above components, the following rules apply:
 Components must be of a single color. For example, individual cubes should not be green on some sides and blue on others. With the exception of coins, all components must be identical colors on all sides.
 You may use any variety in the size and color of components (i.e. 3 small green cubes and 5 large green cubes), but be aware that some players may not have access to a wide assortment of components.
 Components must be unmodified. i.e. You may not use custom markings on the cubes or discs.

The 24 component limit may be made up of any combination of the above components. A few examples:
 4 six-sided dice, 4 eight-sided dice, 6 blue cubes, 4 coins, and 6 red cubes
 2 small coins, 4 plastic discs, 4 metal paper clips, 4 cubes, 2 meeple, and 8 six sided dice in any color.
 10 blue cubes (note that you may have less than 24components)
 24 six sided dice and 2 cups (note that cups do not count toward the 24 component limit).
 You can have no components if you want and only have a card only game."

text:
REFERENCE SHEET
The rule book may have a reference sheet as the last sheet in the rules for gaming information, charts, diagrams, and tables, but it may not be used as a game component. This means you can't place components on it or have it act as a component during game play. (i.e. The player should be able to play the game without the rule book once the rules are learned, yet can be referenced during play for rule refresher purposes.)
All games can have a single reference sheet/player aid in PDF format and double-sided that can be placed on the game table next to the card and used during game play.
 The reference sheet can be no larger than 8.5x11 inches but can be smaller in size "poker sized" or A4 (11.7 x 8.3)
 If your reference sheet is poker card sized, it can be double-sided.
 The reference sheet can not be used as a component where other components would be played on it or around it and it can't be used as a player device for the game; it is only a reference.
 The reference sheet is not considered part of the component list.
 Player aids may not contain rules not found in the rule book or be used as components in play. Player aids do not count toward the 24 component limit.
 It would be advisable to have your reference sheet in the same file as the rules so that it is associated with the rules and how it would be used during game play.

text:
VOTING

Voting will be conducted by rating the games via an online form at Google Forms.
A link to it will be announced and prominently displayed when the Voting Phase begins.

Anyone with a BGG account, and that played, read the rules, looked at components or followed the work-in-progress threads, can participate and vote.
You don't need an entry in the contest, nor have to be a designer to give feedback and to rate the games that you played.

Voters will be required to include their BGG username when they vote, to help prevent accidental or intentional multi-votes and to award voter microbadges.
However, your votes will be kept secret and will not be linked back to your username.

Votes are ratings, not rankings, and each vote for each game is independent.
You don't need to play all the games (or even most) to vote, and you can start voting even if you plan to play more games later.
If for whatever reason you want to change your vote for an entry, simply submit another vote with your user for the same game, and the previous vote will be replaced.

The voting algorithm takes the following factors into consideration:
 Whether you only looked at rules/thread, or played the game.
 Whether you gave feedback to a particular game or not, and how much feedback you gave throughout the contest.
 How many different games you voted for.

Your vote is not affected by the algorithm, only its weight.

Also important to note:
 Since it's a requirement for the contest, if you're a designer and don't give feedback to other games, your game will be downgraded.
Please reach out to me in private if you want to discuss this point.
If you give feedback out of the game's thread (i.e. by geekmail, on comments on google drive, etc), please send me a note, so it's counted.

text:
SUBMITTING AN ENTRY

To submit your game to the contest, please complete each of the steps detailed below.
If your game was not submitted through the form, or is not in this geeklist, it's not in the contest!

Please read this post carefully before creating your entry.
To enter the contest:
1. Create a "work in progress" (WIP) thread in the Works in Progress forum.
 In the top post of your WIP thread, include all the relevant information for your game, and links to the latest PnP and rules. Keep that post updated.
2. You must enter your game's information in the submission form (see instructions within the form).
 Please keep the confirmation email, in case you want to update your information later.
3. You must add your WIP thread to the contest geeklist (see instructions on the header of the geeklist).
 Comments are disabled in the list. As your game develops, please discuss it within its WIP thread.
4. If you change your game's information (name, main image, designer, artist, status, etc), please submit the form again so the changes are updated on my side.
 If you need to withdraw your game, for whatever reason, simply send me a geekmail. If possible, post a note about it on your WIP and on the contest's thread to inform everyone else that the game was withdrawn, but that's entirely optional.

 If you post your WIP in a different forum, this will not disqualify your submission, but you will receive more traffic and feedback if you post to the proper forum.
 Include all the relevant information for your game, and links to the latest PnP and rules:
* game title
* designer/artist/graphic designer credits
* a link back to the contest's thread (enter "[thread=3276117][/thread]" somewhere in your post)
* a short paragraph describing your game
* an image or photo of your game
* a link or links to the latest version of the PnP files and rules once they become available.
 Keep your top WIP post updated, relatively short and attractive. It's your game's presentation card, and the only thing that most visitors will see of your game!
 You may (should) introduce your game to the rest of the participants by posting a brief intro and a link to your WIP thread by replying in this thread. This will help subscribers find out about your game (not everyone follows the geeklist or the WIP forum).
 As your game develops, please discuss it within its WIP thread, not on the contest's thread or in the entry geeklist. To give feedback on a game, also do it in its WIP thread.
 You are welcome, and even encouraged, to post major announcements about your game to the main thread. Some promotion is allowed, but no spam, please (i.e. don't post the same thing over and over, or every minor change).
 Entrants are responsible for ensuring the information on the WIP, on the geeklist, through the submission form, or anywhere else relevant to the contest, is kept up to date. This includes name, credits, status, description.
 The geeklist might be re-sorted from time to time. Please accept an apology for making it a bit harder to find your entry, but it's in an effort to keep the contest fair.

text:
COPYRIGHT
At all times all the rights to your game stay with you.
Rest assured that this is a very friendly and creative community and nobody is going to steal your ideas.
The only requirement is (obviously) that anyone should be able to legally print and assemble their own copies for personal use, for free, for the duration of the contest.
After the voting closes, you may remove access to any and all free versions of your game, and/or provide a paid version, but whoever built a copy of your game should not be required to pay for, or destroy their copy.

Please make sure that you have rights to all artwork, icons, etc. used in your game.
There are a range of web sites to source images and icons that are free to use; there is no need to violate anyone else's copyrights.
When using Creative Commons artwork, please credit the original artist(s) in your rules, or wherever you deem appropriate.

text:
IMPORTANT INFO FOR AI AND ITS USE IN THIS CONTEST

With the releases of MidJourney, Dall-E, ChatGPT, Bard, etc. a host of discussions have been raised around them throughout different game design groups (and many other places, but keeping it relevant).
Truth is, there are many implications, both in the input (what's being used to train the AIs) and the output (how much of the work of a person can they replace, and can they replace some jobs).

This section is new, as I wanted to be clear on the rules around using AI for the purposes of this contest, but as things change these rules might change, to adapt to new legislation, or rulings, in different countries.

As of the start of this contest:
 Using AI for any purpose is allowed, except for designing the game.
 While mentioning that you used AI for something is not required, lying about you doing the work (if discovered), when it was produced by an AI, will be the basis for an immediate disqualification from the contest.
This will be seen as you plagiarizing someone else's texts, art, or mechanisms, without proper credit.
Please be honest if someone asks, and don't try to participate, for instance, in Best Artist if you are not the artist.
 While having honest, adult discussions about AI and all its implications, neither this thread or each individual WIP are places for it.
There are many forums for this, one of which was opened just before the start of the 2023 contest:  . Please go there to discuss those matters, or create your own thread/blog/forum.
 It should be implied by the rule above, but I want to make it clear: Complaining or making comments about a game or designer using AI, or starting arguments on why it's good and bad about it is not allowed in this contest.
 We all have an opinion about AI. Even not caring one way or the other is an opinion. Keep your opinions to the relevant forums, and be respectful. If you don't like an entry because they use AI, simply ignore that entry.
Comments denigrating, bullying or in any form criticizing a game or person for using AI will be reported to BGG. Hopefully we won't have to do that.

If you have questions or comments regarding these rules, use the forums mentioned. If you want to reach out to me to know my opinion, I can share it privately (both as someone that works in IT, someone that is married to an art teacher, a game designer, and someone that enjoys writing), but I'm also not looking to convince anyone or be convinced of anything. 

I hope these rules can be refined and perfected as we progress, either for this or for future/other contests.

text:
Thematic/Mechanic category: BEST CARD-ONLY GAME

This is an award reserved for games that don't require ANY components, other than the single card of the game and the rulebook.
The optional reference sheet is not considered a component, and therefore it doesn't exclude a game from participating in the card-only category.

The winners are:
#1: Word Wheel  by D. Teuber
#2: Fruits & Veggies  by Christy Castro
#3: Pythagoras  by Marcos Maldonado
#4: At the Mesas of Madness  by Joem Antonio
#5: Index Fusion  by David Nagy
#6: Sho’gloth snags some snacks  by maf
#7: The magic well  by Agustín Atencio Andrioli
#8: Battle of Reflexes  by Arjit Raj
#9: Tic Tic BOOM!  by Marcos Maldonado
#10: Labyrinthio  by Pasko

Tips were 2 to the prize pot for Best Card-Only Game. The total for prizes is 54.12.
